stem: A healthcare operations study measures the wait time (minutes) for a sample of 30 emergency room visitors. The sample mean is 20.4 min with a sample standard deviation of 8.4 min. However, 3 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 27 observations have a mean of 19.1 min and standard deviation of 5.4 min. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 20.4, 95% CI = [17.3, 23.5]. Without outliers: mean = 19.1, 95% CI = [17.0, 21.2]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [17.0, 23.5]. Point estimate: 19.8 min.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [17.0, 23.5].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
